messages:
deploy-bot: started rollout of model-abacus@v2.3.0 to prod (region: us-west) — canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%. changelist: https://git.internal/r/model-abacus/commit/8f3a9b
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident triggered: GPU-pool-exhaustion (severity: high). Paging eng-sre oncall: @alex. Auto-signal: queue_length > 4000 for 6m
alex: seeing the page. joining. any customer-facing alerts?
support-bot: 1 customer complaining of 503s (org: AcmeRetail). Error spike started ~2m after canary bump.
maria: checking infra metrics now — pulling gpux queue histograms
sam: possible model change note in changelist: "kv-cache eviction policy changed to LRU and context-max default bumped to 16384" — could be context growth.
maria: metrics snippet:
```
time       gpu_pool.queue_length  gpu_pool.util
2031456760  1200                  68%
2031456780  2800                  91%
2031456800  5100                  98%
2031456820  6400                  99%
```
alex: holy — queue jumping fast. autoscaler didn't add nodes, hitting max_scale 8.
ben: autoscaler logs:
```
[2031456815] scale_decision: desired=12, max_allowed=8 -> throttle
[2031456820] backoff: 30s
[2031456830] queue_length=6200, avg_latency=2300ms
```
seema: any quick mitigations? can we rollback the canary or pin traffic?
alex: yes. options: (1) pause rollout + shift traffic back to v2.2.8 (2) increase max_scale (but provisioning takes 3-6m) (3) force-serving-mode: kv-cache disabled for v2.3.0 (hotpatch)
maria: I can pause rollout now with redwoodctl: `redwoodctl rollout pause model-abacus v2.3.0 --region us-west`
sam: I'd prefer traffic pin to v2.2.8 while we triage — less risk. v2.3.0 seems to be expanding context retention which explains kv-cache growth and memory pressure.
alex: do the traffic pin and pause. maria, can you run the pause and confirm the canary is rolled back to 10% or lower?
maria: running commands now:
```
$ redwoodctl rollout pause model-abacus v2.3.0 --region us-west
✅ rollout paused
$ redwoodctl traffic set model-abacus --version v2.2.8 --percent 100 --region us-west
✅ traffic updated: v2.2.8=100%
```
alex: confirmed. queue_length dropping?
maria: watching metrics:
```
2031456840 queue_length=4200 util=85%
2031456850 queue_length=1800 util=60%
2031456860 queue_length=700  util=35%
```
ben: autoscaler back to normal decision horizon. no more throttles in last 30s.
support-bot: AcmeRetail reports traffic recovering; still seeing occasional 502s for a few users — reopen if continues.
sam: root cause hypothesis: v2.3.0 defaulted to context-max=16384 and disabled aggressive kv eviction; under typical request patterns this triples per-request KV memory leading to longer decode time and throttled queues. Also increased prefix caching hit churn.
alex: next steps (actionable):
- revert config that bumped context-max in the next patch
- run synthetic load test with long-context traces before re-rollout
- add autoscaler safety: alert when desired>max_allowed for >2min
- postmortem and customer impact note
maria: I'll open an infra ticket to bump max_scale for progressive rollouts and add a faster-provision buffer.
ben: I'll add a temporary incident label and handoff note for next oncall. assigning to @ben for 2hr watch.
ben: taking watch. brief summary: paused v2.3.0, pinned traffic to v2.2.8, queue metrics normalized. investigating kv-cache changes with @sam.
seema: I'll draft a customer comms update for impacted accounts with timeline.
sam: digging into commit 8f3a9b now, will propose a hotfix to restore previous eviction policy. ETA 90m.
alex: thanks everyone. handing off to @ben. if spike recurs ping pager and escalate to infra lead. :thumbsup:
ben: acknowledged — will update thread and escalate if >5% error rate persists for 15m.
incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. closed pager to oncall. incident id: INC-2031456789
